title: Citric acid, 21 CFR 184.1033: direct food substances affirmed as generally recognized as safe
journal: Code of Federal Regulations, title 21, section 184.1033 (59 FR 63895, 12 December 1994), read in the electronic Code of Federal Regulations, up to date as of 20 October 2026
funder: US Food and Drug Administration; the text is federal regulation codified by the Office of the Federal Register.
result: Part 184 lists direct food substances affirmed as generally recognized as safe. Citric acid (C6H8O7, CAS 77-92-9) is 2-hydroxy-1,2,3-propanetricarboxylic acid, a naturally occurring constituent of plant and animal tissues. It may be produced by recovery from sources such as lemon or pineapple juice, by mycological fermentation using Candida spp. (21 CFR 173.160 and 173.165) and by the solvent extraction process of 21 CFR 173.280 for recovery from Aspergillus niger fermentation liquor. It meets Food Chemicals Codex specifications and, in accordance with 21 CFR 184.1(b)(1), is used in food with no limitations other than current good manufacturing practice.
